authoredPrompt: This figure is a potential energy curve for a pair of hydrogen atoms, drawn on a pale blue field with small green spheres added to show the atomic arrangement at three points along it. A tall gradient arrow at the far left, shaded from cream to orange and labeled Energy, gives the sense of the vertical scale, while the plot's own vertical axis is marked only with a plus sign, a 0, and a minus sign, with a horizontal dashed line drawn across at zero. The horizontal axis is labeled Internuclear distance and ends in a magenta arrow pointing right. One magenta curve drops steeply from the upper left, crosses below zero, reaches a rounded minimum, then rises gradually and levels off toward the zero line at large separation. At the top of the steep branch two green spheres overlap, annotated HH (too close). At the right, two widely separated spheres sit above a magenta dashed line joining the letters H and H, annotated H - - - H (too far). At the bottom of the well two just-touching spheres are labeled H-H, and a short vertical dashed line drops from the minimum to the axis, tagged 74 pm, with a green arrow labeled Bond length pointing to it. The depth and position of the single minimum, read against the two extremes flanking it, mark the separation at which attraction and nuclear repulsion balance and fix the length of a covalent bond.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for internuclear distance: learner drags the two hydrogen atoms closer or farther apart, and a point moves along the energy curve from too close through the 74 pm minimum to too far, showing that bond length occurs where attraction and repulsion balance.
- Click for curve regions: learner clicks the repulsive wall, energy well, or far-separated tail, and the corresponding atom sketch is highlighted, making clear why energy rises at very short distance, falls at bonding distance, and approaches zero when atoms separate.
authoredContext:
How close are the two nuclei in the H2 molecule? If they are too close, they will repel each other because both are positively charged. Yet if they’re too far apart, they won’t be able to share the bonding electrons. Thus, there is an optimum distance between nuclei that leads to maximum stability (the figure). Called the bond length, this distance is 74 pm in the H–H molecule. Every covalent bond has both a characteristic bond strength and bond length.

A plot of energy versus internuclear distance for two hydrogen atoms. The distance between nuclei at the minimum energy point is the bond length.

A graph of energy versus internuclear distance. A horizontal line separates the positive and negative energy and a curve with a single trough at 74 ppm is shown.

discrepancies: the generated default view adds a yellow highlight halo around the bonded H–H atoms and a magenta/white current-point marker at the curve minimum, neither of which appears in the source static figure
clickable curve-region highlights are implemented as a thick yellow overlay path/halos that can visually alter the source-style diagram rather than preserving the clean textbook curve by default

the advertised click regions for repulsive wall, well, and far tail do not move the slider/current point to those regions, so the interaction is only partly tied to the displayed internuclear-distance state
the source's clean static composition is slightly cluttered by the persistent interactive marker and active well emphasis around the 74 pm atoms
evaluation.notes: The figure is highly recognizable with the correct H2 potential-energy curve, labels, colors, and bond-length annotation, but the default state includes extra interactive highlighting/markers that make it less like a drop-in replacement for the original static image.
action_items: Remove or greatly reduce the default yellow halo around the bonded atoms so the initial view matches the unhighlighted source figure more closely.
Make the magenta current-point marker optional, smaller, or hidden until the slider is used, since the source does not mark the curve minimum with a target symbol.
When users click the repulsive wall, well, or far tail, update the slider value and move the current point to a representative distance in that region rather than only showing a popup/highlight.
Keep any yellow curve-region highlight hidden by default and show it only transiently after interaction.
